comments.content: The original code `"adapter.body.{}.".format(i, j)` was a bug (extra unused argument), but the fix `"adapter.body.{}.".format(i, )` is equivalent to `"adapter.body.{}.".format(i)`. The trailing comma is harmless but unnecessary. More importantly, verify this is the intended key: the loop variable `j` is now unused in this line, which is correct if the original intent was to map `adapter.body.{i}.` to `body.{i*2}.`. However, note that the previous line already maps `adapter.body.{i}.resnets.{j}.` to `body.{i*2+j}.`, so this line handles the non-resnet body keys. This looks correct.

Moving `clip` to the top of the required inputs changes the node's input ordering, which will break existing workflows that rely on positional input order (e.g., API-format prompts or serialized workflows). This is a backward-incompatible change. Consider keeping `clip` at its original position or providing a migration path.

Enabling the entire `F` rule set (Pyflakes) is broader than the previous `F401`/`F841` selection and includes `F821` (undefined-name), which the previous comment explicitly noted had 7 remaining errors. This will likely cause CI/lint failures. Either fix the remaining `F821` errors in this PR or keep `F821` disabled until they are addressed.

The second cell still uses `time.sleep(0.5)` but the `import time` was removed from this cell. If this cell is executed independently (which is common in Colab notebooks), it will raise `NameError: name 'time' is not defined`. Either re-add `import time` here or ensure the earlier cell that imports it is always run first.
